title: The Pandaren Started as an April Fools Joke
hook: Blizzard announced the pandaren as an April Fools prank in 2002. Ten years later the panda expansion sold 2.7 million copies in a week. Did you ever roll a pandaren?
script: Did you know the pandaren started as an April Fools joke? On April 1, 2002, Blizzard announced a fifth playable race for Warcraft Three. The post introduced the mighty Pandaren Empire, complete with fake lore, fake units and a fake hero. The art came from Samwise Didier, a longtime Blizzard art director whose own nickname was Panda. It was all a prank. The joke landed harder than anyone expected. Fans loved the panda warriors, and some of them believed the announcement was real. So Blizzard kept them around. A year later, The Frozen Throne added the Pandaren Brewmaster as a neutral hero, and Chen Stormstout showed up in the bonus campaign. Years went by, and designer Dave Kosak said a playable pandaren race became by far the most requested feature in World of Warcraft. At BlizzCon on October 21, 2011, Chris Metzen revealed Mists of Pandaria. It launched on September 25, 2012, and sold 2.7 million copies in its first week. The pandaren became the first race that could join either the Horde or the Alliance. Plenty of players still assumed the whole expansion was an elaborate prank. Not bad for a joke.
